intro: Notion works well for product managers on a Mac. You can write PRDs, keep meeting notes, and run a light backlog from linked databases in the Notion desktop app for macOS 13 or later. This guide covers setup, the shortcuts that save the most time, the plan limits, and the gaps you will hit. It also shows where Lazur helps and where it does not.
tldr: Install the Mac app from notion.com/desktop. It needs macOS 13 or later.
Learn ⌘P, ⌘T, and ⇧⌘N first. They move you between pages and windows fastest.
Build the backlog as one database, then link each PRD and meeting note to its row.
Notion has no built-in public roadmap, voting, or RICE scoring. Plan a workaround before your first review.
Lazur sees your screen while you hold ⌥ ⌘, answers out loud, and guides you one click at a time.

blocks.text: Product managers on a Mac use Notion for the same few jobs. They write PRDs and specs. They take meeting notes. They build a team wiki. They run a light backlog and roadmap from linked databases. A third-party product management blog says this works for very early teams, and it lists the same jobs. This guide covers each one, plus the limits you will hit.
Install the Notion desktop app on your Mac

Start at notion.com/desktop. Click Download for macOS and open the file you download. Notion updates the app on its own. You can also check by hand. Use the menu bar's Check for Updates item if a feature looks missing.

items: Open the Apple menu > About This Mac and check your macOS version.
Go to notion.com/desktop and click Download for macOS.
Open the downloaded file and launch Notion.
Sign in and open the workspace your team uses.
Open Settings > Preferences and review the options before you start.

blocks.text: The app needs macOS 13 or later. Notion's system requirements page lists no hardware requirements for desktop. If your Mac runs an older system, use Notion in a browser instead. If your company controls installs, your IT team can manage the update settings.

blocks.title: Test on one Mac first
blocks.text: Install the app on one Mac and open your main workspace. Check the sidebar, search, and sign-in. Then send the setup steps to the rest of the team.
Which Notion plan fits a product team

Notion charges per member per month. The Free plan costs $0 and caps file uploads at 5 MB per file. Plus costs $10 per member per month and raises the file limit to 5 GB. Business costs $20 per member per month, with the same 5 GB limit. Business also includes AI Meeting Notes and Enterprise Search (Beta).

blocks.text: Notion's pricing page gives no block limit for teams of two or more members. It also gives no numeric AI usage caps. Read the page again before you commit a team, because plans change.

blocks.title: Big files fail on Free
blocks.text: A 5 MB limit blocks most screen recordings and design exports. Store the large file in your team's storage app and link to it from the PRD.
Notion keyboard shortcuts on Mac that save PM time
Most product managers use a small set of shortcuts every day. These come from Notion's keyboard shortcut page. Learn them in this order, starting with the ones that move you between pages.

items: ⌘P or ⌘K: search, or jump back to a page you opened recently.
⌘F: find text inside the page you have open.
⌘N: create a new page.
⇧⌘N: open a new Notion window. Keep the spec in one window and the backlog in another.
⌘T: create a new tab.
⌘ click a link: open the link in a new tab.
⌥ ⇧ click a page: open the page as a new window.

blocks.text: Start with ⌘P. A PM jumps between a PRD, a backlog, and a meeting page many times a day. Search is faster than hunting through the sidebar. Use ⌘T when you want a second page without losing the first.

blocks.title: Turn off the search tab
blocks.text: New tabs open a search window by default. To change that, go to Settings > Preferences and switch off Open Search when creating a new tab. You open the page you meant to open.
A common mistake is copying a shortcut list from a blog and never checking it. Shortcuts can change. When a key does nothing, open Notion's keyboard shortcut page and compare.
Turn on the Notion desktop beta for faster tabs

The desktop beta changes how tabs work on Mac. All tabs in one window share a single running copy of Notion. Notion says this makes switching faster, keeps the sidebar in place, and uses less memory. The beta needs desktop app version 7.39.0 or later.

To join, click Try Desktop Beta in the tab bar. You can also go to Settings > Preferences > Desktop beta. Notion restarts each time you join or leave. To leave, click the Beta button in the tab bar and choose Leave beta, or turn off Desktop beta in Settings.

Each beta window holds one workspace. A window with several workspaces splits apart, and tab groups become separate windows. A PM who works in a company workspace and a side project workspace will see two windows after joining. Plan for that before a busy day.

blocks.title: Save drafts before you switch
blocks.text: Joining or leaving the beta restarts Notion. Finish your edit and wait for the page to save before you change the setting.
Write a PRD in Notion that engineers actually read

A good PRD is short enough to read in one sitting. Put the decision at the top. Put the detail below it. Engineers scan for what changed, what is out of scope, and what they must answer before work starts. Use this structure.

rows: Problem
Who has the problem, and what it costs them today.
Writing the solution before the problem.
Goals and non goals
What success looks like, and what this work will not do.
Leaving out non goals, so scope grows.
Success measure
One metric, who owns it, and where it is read.
Listing many metrics with no owner.
Open questions
Each question with the person who will answer it.
Burying unknowns in the body text.
Rollout
Who sees the change first, and how to roll it back.
No rollback plan at all.
blocks.caption: A PRD structure that engineers can scan quickly.

blocks.text: Here is a worked example. This example is made up. A PM writes a PRD for reminders that fire on the Mac. The problem is that people miss due tasks shared with their team. The non goal is an Android app this quarter. The open question is whether sync with Apple Reminders is in scope. An engineer answers that before any build starts.
Use toggles for long background research. Readers open them when they need the detail. Keep the top of the page clear for people who only read the first screen.

blocks.title: Draft, then check
blocks.text: Ask Lazur to draft the outline, then fill in the facts yourself. Lazur does not know your customers or your data. Keep only numbers and quotes you can source.
Build a product backlog in one Notion database

A backlog in Notion works best as one database. Each row is one idea, bug, or project. Link each row to its PRD and its meeting notes. One database is easier to filter than several pages. It also keeps rows from getting lost.
Start small. Add properties only when a review needs them. These properties cover most PM backlogs.

items: Status: a select property with values such as Idea, Spec, Building, and Shipped.
Owner: a person property, so each row has one name.
Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort: number properties for scoring.
Spec: a relation to the PRD page, so you jump from the row to the doc.
Score: a formula property that combines the scoring fields.

blocks.text: Notion does not score RICE for you. Type the formula into a formula property: prop("Reach") * prop("Impact") * prop("Confidence") / prop("Effort"). Each name must match your property name exactly, including capital letters.

Large databases slow down. A third-party blog says the slowdown becomes noticeable as a database grows past hundreds of items. Treat that as a warning, not a benchmark. Filter your main view to Status is not Shipped, and archive shipped rows at the end of each cycle.
Plan a roadmap in Notion without a timeline view

Roadmaps are the weakest part of Notion for product work. A third-party review says Notion has no native timeline or Gantt view. Check the view menu on your database before you build a workaround. Views can change, and a timeline option may already be there.

If no timeline option exists, group a Board view by quarter. Add a select property called Quarter. Each card then sits in one column per quarter. Use a Calendar view for launches with a fixed date. A launch on the calendar is easier to see than a date in a table.

Notion's official Product Management Roadmap template is free. It was made by Akshay Raveendran and has a 5.0 rating from 5 ratings. The template page does not describe its databases or views. Duplicate a copy and read it before you rely on it.

blocks.title: No public roadmap built in
blocks.text: Notion has no built-in feedback portal, voting, or public roadmap. If customers need to vote, use a separate tool and link to it from a Notion page.

blocks.text: These gaps come from one third-party blog and a few reviews. No survey of product managers backs them up. Test each gap in your own workspace before you decide anything. A gap that never touches your team is not a gap for you.
Teams that need timelines and cycles often pair Notion with another planning tool. See [Linear for product managers on Mac](/for/product-managers/linear) for that side of the work.
Dictate meeting notes into Notion on Mac

Hold fn to dictate. Lazur turns your speech into clean, formatted text at the cursor, in any app, Notion included. Snippets handle text you repeat. A personal dictionary holds product names and teammate names. Clipboard slots keep text you reuse.

Here is a worked example. You leave a call about a checkout bug. Hold fn and read your rough notes out loud. Put your feature names in the personal dictionary before the call, so they come out spelled right every time.

Notion's pricing page says Business includes AI Meeting Notes. If your team is on Business, check that feature first. Dictation fits when a call was not recorded, or when you want your own words on the page.
Ask Lazur about a Notion page on Mac

Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.
Lazur does not click for you. It does not edit your pages or operate other apps. It is not a plugin or add-in for Notion. You make every change yourself, in the page you already have open.

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Keep that in mind when a page holds customer data. The [Notion page for Lazur](/apps/notion) has more on drafts and shortcuts.
Mistakes product managers make with Notion on Mac

items: Splitting the backlog into many databases with no relations. Search then becomes guesswork.
Uploading large files to the Free plan. The 5 MB limit blocks them. Link to storage instead.
Skipping updates. Notion updates itself, but a stale app can miss fixes. Check for updates when something looks wrong.
Joining the desktop beta the week of a launch. Joining restarts the app and changes the window layout.
Writing every PRD from scratch. Keep one template page and duplicate it.
Typing scores as plain text. A formula keeps the score right when an input changes.

blocks.text: Most of these come from habit, not missing features. Fix the habit first, then judge the tool.
Your Notion on Mac setup checklist

items: Install the desktop app and confirm your Mac runs macOS 13 or later.
Open Settings > Preferences and decide on Open Search when creating a new tab.
Create the backlog database with Status, Owner, and Spec properties.
Duplicate one PRD and fill in the table sections for a live feature.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur one question about that page.

blocks.text: The Lazur trial starts when you first open the app, and it needs no credit card. Download Lazur for Mac from the [download page](/download). To see how Lazur fits PM work, read the [product managers page](/for/product-managers).

faq.question: Is Notion free for product managers on Mac?
faq.answer: The Free plan costs $0 per member per month. Its file uploads are capped at 5 MB per file, and Notion AI features on Free are trials. Plus costs $10 per member per month with 5 GB uploads. Business costs $20 per member per month and adds AI Meeting Notes. Check Notion's pricing page before you choose.

faq.question: Which macOS version does the Notion desktop app need?
faq.answer: The Notion desktop app needs macOS 13 or later, according to Notion's system requirements page. That page lists no hardware requirements for desktop. If your Mac runs an older system, use Notion in a browser.

faq.question: Does Notion have a timeline or Gantt view for roadmaps?
faq.answer: A third-party blog says Notion has no native timeline or Gantt view. Check the view menu on your database first, since views can change. If nothing fits, use a Board view grouped by quarter or a Calendar view for dated launches.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons or edit my Notion pages?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at things, guides you one click at a time, answers out loud, and drafts or types text. It does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Notion.

faq.question: Does Lazur store what I say or the screenshots it sees?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Why does my large Notion database feel slow?
faq.answer: One third-party blog says slowdowns show up as databases grow past hundreds of items. That is one blog's view, not a benchmark. Filter your main view to open items, and archive shipped rows at the end of each cycle to keep the working set small.

faq.question: Does the Notion desktop beta use less memory on Mac?
faq.answer: Notion says the desktop beta shares one running copy across tabs, and that this uses less memory. Notion's January 20, 2026 release notes also say Mac desktop is up +11%, a self-reported figure with no method given. Test the beta on your own Mac before you rely on it.
